name: Elithia
long_description:
US workers' compensation paid out $64.1 billion in 2023. Personal injury, malpractice, and other insurance claims add billions more. Behind every one of these claims sit thousands of pages of medical records, and a clinician spends hours or days reading them to reconstruct what happened to the patient.

Elithia is building agents to do this work.

Our agents reconstruct patient histories, reason across conflicting evidence, and produce defensible analyses, with every finding cited to the original record.

We've sold to physician expert witnesses and medical-legal firms, turning thousands of pages into court-ready chronologies an expert can verify in minutes. Next: TPAs and insurers, where the same review sits behind every injury claim.

launches.tagline: A day of medical-record review, done in 15 minutes
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Elithia's agents are medical reviewers. They read the records behind a malpractice or serious injury case the way a junior doctor would, and hand the expert a report and chronology with every line cited to the source page. A day of reading, done in 15 minutes. 70+ physician experts already work with it. **[Book a 20-minute demo](https://calendly.com/sarthak-minerva/30min)** or **[run your next case free](https://studio.elithia.com/signup)**.

https://youtu.be/U2Fn-jouJAs

### The problem

Every injury claim buys the same unit of labor: a clinically trained person reading the record. A single malpractice or catastrophic injury file is thousands of pages, out of order and full of duplicates. A doctor, nurse or paralegal spends days on it, at thousands of dollars a case, before anyone knows whether there is a case at all.

In the US, personal injury law firms earn $61.7 billion a year (IBISWorld, 2025), and workers' compensation pays $64.1 billion in benefits, $30.3 billion of it for medical care (NASI, 2023). Nearly every one of those claims turns on what the medical records say.

### How Elithia works

Hand Elithia the records the way you would hand them to a junior. It removes blanks and duplicates, sorts and dates every document, reconstructs the patient history, and reasons across conflicting evidence. It comes back with a chronology where every finding links to the page it came from, so the expert can check it in minutes and sign off. Export to Word or PDF, in a secure workspace geofenced to your region.

Elithia does the reading. The judgment stays with the expert.

### Why this compounds

Software sold to law firms gives a paralegal a faster way to do the reading. Elithia does the reading itself, and it works alongside the physicians who give the expert opinion and have to defend it under cross-examination. Like any junior, it gets better with every case a senior corrects: each chronology a physician checks and signs off teaches Elithia what a specialist in that field treats as relevant.

### Where we are

- 70+ physician expert witnesses use Elithia on live cases.
- Two medico-legal agencies (firms that supply expert reports to law firms) are under contract.
- Next: law firms on both sides of malpractice and catastrophic injury cases.

### Team

I'm Sarthak. I grew up in a family of doctors, then spent three years as a quant developer at a $19B fund turning unstructured data into trading signals (Oxford CS '21). I left MIT Sloan's MBA to point the same machinery at medicine.

### Our ask

- **Run a malpractice, birth injury, nursing home or catastrophic injury practice, plaintiff or defense?** Send us your worst file. [Book a 20-minute demo](https://calendly.com/sarthak-minerva/30min) or email **sarthak@elithia.com**.
- **Physician or nurse expert writing reports?** [Run your next case free](https://studio.elithia.com/signup), with your first 1,000 pages on us.
- **Know a litigation partner or a head of claims at an insurer?** We'd love an intro.
